challenges.name: build-push-traceable-image
challenges.title: Build the image on every pull request, push it with traceable tags
challenges.description: Until now the api image was built on a laptop and pushed as `latest`, so nobody could tell which commit ran on the VPS, and a rollback meant rebuilding an old commit. The first workflow that replaced it also pushed from pull requests and failed for pull requests from forks. The editor holds `.github/workflows/image.yml` with its key blocks missing, each marked by a `# [ ]` line; some pieces are wrong on purpose. Fill every line so that: the workflow runs for pull requests into `main`, pushes to `main` and tags like `v1.4.0`, and nothing else; the token can read the repository and write packages, and the login to `ghcr.io` uses that token (no personal token, no other secret is set in this repository); a pull request builds the image but signs in to nothing and pushes nothing; every image carries a `sha-<7 chars>` tag, plus the branch name on a push to main, `pr-<number>` on a pull request, and `1.4.0`, `1.4` and `latest` on the release tag `v1.4.0`; the build uses `api/` as its context and the GitHub Actions cache (`type=gha`, `mode=max` on export). Run grades the file with a simulator of the trigger filters, the token and the three Docker actions.
hints: Follow one event at a time through the steps: on a pull request, which steps run, what does `push:` evaluate to, and what would a push without a login answer? On the tag push, which `tags:` lines of the metadata step produce something?

Look at `tags:` next to `branches:` under `push`, the `packages` scope in `permissions:`, the `if:` of the login step, the `type=` lines of `docker/metadata-action` (it adds `latest` by itself on a release), and an expression for `push:` instead of a constant.

An image for the `web/` folder that builds on pull requests into `develop` and pushes only from `develop`: `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'` on the login, metadata `tags: |` with `type=sha` and `type=ref,event=branch`, and `push: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}` with `tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}` on the build.

tests.name: A push to main signs in and pushes the image tagged with the branch and the short commit
A pull request builds the image but signs in to nothing and pushes nothing
The release tag v1.4.0 pushes 1.4.0, 1.4, latest and the short commit
A feature branch push starts nothing; a pull request from a fork still builds
The token reads the repository and writes packages, and it is what signs in
The build uses api/ and the GitHub Actions cache
